historical_job_control_revalidation.cause: Stopped-job completion raced SIGCHLD; token matching consumed the following prompt boundary.
historical_job_control_revalidation.fix: Observe foreground ownership and signal masks; retry the stopped-job wait status in a bounded builtin loop until it reports termination; preserve the next prompt boundary after a completion token.
historical_job_control_revalidation.counting: At the original baseline snapshot of 199 modern fixtures, replace the six canonical job-control records with their revalidated results. Repeats add confidence, not unique case coverage. The other 193 baseline fixture definitions were byte-identical; later migration fixtures are separate additions.

failed_records.operation: utf8 normalize NFC|NFD|NFKC|NFKD; all 20 column conditions per line

exclusions.detail: utf8 exposes only full default case folding and default case mappings. Simple (S) and Turkic (T) folds, and language-conditional SpecialCasing entries, have no candidate interface; Final_Sigma is covered by unicode17-final-sigma.

U+0000 is a scalar value but cannot appear in a Bash argument (C strings end at NUL). Its 8 sweep assertions (NFC, NFD, NFKC, NFKD invariance, casefold, lower, upper, title) are not executed; GraphemeBreakTest exclusions are in unicode17-grapheme-nul-unrepresentable. NormalizationTest, CaseFolding and the malformed vectors contain no U+0000.
GraphemeBreakTest lines containing U+0000 cannot be passed through Bash argv (C strings end at NUL); they are excluded from every grapheme assertion, not passed.

retained_behavioral_failures.oracle: OpenSSH server and client with fixture-only generated Ed25519 host/client keys and strict known_hosts. Setup queries client-supported algorithms, proves both algorithms actually connect to a permissive OpenSSH server, and proves allowed success/disallowed negotiation refusal against a restricted OpenSSH server. MACs hmac-sha2-256 vs hmac-sha2-512 and KEX curve25519-sha256 vs diffie-hellman-group14-sha256 are forced explicitly. The MAC case uses aes256-ctr and both direction-specific debug negotiation lines must name the selected real MAC. The separate KEX case uses chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com and verifies its implicit MAC, which supplies no evidence for the explicit MAC requirement. Banner is absent because static95 found a pre-auth protocol blocker. Each candidate run requires its own successful allowed command; parser/startup/cipher/authentication rejection cannot substitute for the intended policy obligation.
retained_behavioral_failures.comparison: Exact semantic booleans for allowed encrypted command success, expected negotiated cipher/MAC/KEX, disallowed client status255 at the matching negotiation phase, no command marker, normal server teardown and no forced cleanup. The disallowed policy boolean is gated by successful allowed negotiation and command execution, even when raw refusal text is present. All raw ssh -vv client transcripts, statuses, configurations, server logs and owned PID identities are retained outside the compared tree.

retained_behavioral_failures.oracle: Documented bash-os contract (batch_doc and cron_doc): batch reads a script from stdin and queues ${BASHCRON_SPOOL_DIR}/atjobs/<seconds>.<pid>.<seq>.job whose first line is "# run_at=<seconds>"; cron's scanner runs ready jobs in submission (FIFO) order and removes them; "low load" is currently immediate. Expectations are computed by the observer from facts it controls (submitter pids, wall-clock seconds, the order in which it released each submitter, the fixed consumer clock), never from candidate output. Source note: ids sort by strcmp over <sec>.<pid>.<seq>, so within one second the pid text, not submission order, decides (batch.c:116-119, cron.c:865-892).
retained_behavioral_failures.comparison: Two candidate shells are spawned (the first has the lower pid) and each blocks until the observer releases it. The observer releases them in the stated order inside one aligned second (retried until both ids carry the same second), runs one consumer poll with a fixed clock, and compares the execution order with the release order. The last row releases the higher-pid shell first and the lower-pid shell in the following second. Ids, pids, seconds and the log are retained. Every observation is in observations.jsonl; tables, clock and state files, job logs, spool listings and daemon streams stay in the case workspace, which the harness preserves.

retained_behavioral_failures.oracle: Independent kernel oracle: the helper's own NETLINK_GENERIC client (hand-encoded request builder, attribute parser including the nested operation and multicast-group arrays, several messages per buffer, several buffers per dump, NLMSG_DONE/NLMSG_ERROR/ACK handling, sequence and port matching) is first calibrated on hand-encoded vectors and then on the real guest kernel (by name, by id, dump, two interleaved requests, NLM_F_ACK, ENOENT); it is the only source of family IDs, versions, header sizes, operations, capability flags, multicast groups and errno values, so no expected value comes from candidate output. retained_behavioral_failures.oracle: Independent OpenSSH client/server and RFC4253 sections6/7.1/7.3. A byte-preserving loopback relay retains both entire initial streams, exact packet offsets, lengths, padding and hashes. The guarded parser reads version/clear packets and10 name-lists, validates reserved/tail fields, and stops each direction at NEWKEYS; following bytes remain opaque. All peers force non-AEAD aes256-ctr and curve25519-sha256; the actual separate MAC must appear in both raw proposals and client negotiated-direction diagnostics. Setup ssh-Q checks the real client supports both MACs, then OpenSSH independently proves default-allowed, permissive-allowed, permissive-other and restricted-allowed encrypted commands, plus actual restricted-other MAC mismatch/refusal. Candidate repeats all5 probes using fresh fixture keys and strict known_hosts. Standard preserves the revision98 MAC choices; etm exercises another source-advertised real-MAC framing path. Neither variant substitutes implicit AEAD authentication for the MAC requirement.
retained_behavioral_failures.comparison: Exact ordered booleans distinguish advertisement, clear KEX/ECDH/NEWKEYS progress, full encrypted auth/command and policy. Successful encrypted command requires status0, exact marker/stdout, strict fixture host-key verification, authenticated client log and expected non-AEAD cipher/real MAC in both directions. Refusal requires255, the matching MAC diagnostic, both raw MAC intersections empty, other KEX/cipher intersections still valid, no NEWKEYS or command marker. Full policy boolean is gated by successful default, both permissive MACs and restricted-allowed encrypted commands. Raw proposal filtering/early refusal cannot pass that gate if a baseline encryption path fails. Normal server exits, relay thread cleanup and no forced kills remain required. Server phase ports differ; readiness needs the exact Popen child alive plus its own post-bind announcement and the loopback listener, preventing the stale-listener problem observed in109.

retained_behavioral_failures.oracle: Independent protocol oracle. Persistent candidate shells run the UNCHANGED builtin as uid 2000 in private state directories on IPv4 loopback inside the disposable VM. The wire format (1212-byte datagram, BCLSTR2 magic, big-endian port, 32-row table, keyed BLAKE2b-256 over the first 1180 bytes) is the fixture's own implementation on hashlib, validated in setup against BLAKE2b known answers and round trips; oracle peers, probes and decoys are owned UDP sockets that validate every request field by field. Expected values never come from candidate output alone: identities and rosters are cross-checked on the wire (authenticated PONG and ROSTER packets), file contents are parsed independently, timing bounds come from the documented deadline (request deadline, heartbeat every quarter, expiry after three), and kernel facts come from /proc (process tree, UDP table, receive queues), inotify, bind() collisions, modes and owners. Setup controls (a failure is an ERROR, never a candidate result): hashing and codec known answers, loopback delivery of 0/1/1212/65507 byte datagrams, the UDP table and its queues, wildcard decoys, every oracle peer mode, inotify atomicity detection, and the persistent-shell driver (status/stdout/stderr extraction, deadline kill, removal of a child that outlives its shell, reaping). Only processes started by the fixture are signaled; every key is evaluated for every vector, an unevaluated key prints ERROR, and any control or fixture exception prints CONTROL-INVALID and exits 97.
retained_behavioral_failures.comparison: Every key of every vector is evaluated and must be yes. [three-peer-convergence] joins-ok: the seed and two peers started and joined; identities-on-wire: each PONG gives the node id and port, one cluster id, three distinct nodes; rosters-converge: all three members files equal the wire-derived list (seed, peer, peer) within 5 s; members-commands-agree: cluster members prints the same list on each; c-left-status: the third peer leave exits 0; leave-removed-everywhere: the seed and the other peer drop it within 4 s; survivors-intact: both survivors keep their listeners and state=initialized; c-state-cleaned: the leaver state files are gone. [expiry-and-refresh] oracles-joined: two oracle nodes joined the seed next to two candidate peers; silent-expires-not-early: the oracle that never beats leaves the roster no earlier than three deadlines after its join (1.2 s); silent-expires-in-bound: and within three deadlines plus a quarter deadline plus 1.5 s; beating-oracle-retained: the oracle beating every half deadline outlives the silent one by more than two deadlines; beating-peers-retained: the two candidate peers stay in the seed roster at every poll; retention-ends-after-last-beat: the beating oracle expires three deadlines (within the slack) after its last heartbeat; expiry-propagates-to-peers: both candidate peers drop both oracles within 2 s. [seed-loss] peers-joined: seed and leaf joined with equal rosters; seed-left-status: the seed leave exits 0; leaf-disconnected: the leaf state file and status become disconnected within three deadlines plus slack; leaf-roster-self-only: the leaf roster keeps only itself; leaf-listener-alive: the leaf listener is alive; leaf-stopped-after-kill: after SIGKILL of the verified leaf listener, status reports stopped. Retained in the case tree: observations.jsonl (every command with its raw stdout, stderr, status, duration and finish time, every oracle exchange as hex, teardown findings, and r2 trace: the ordered observation timeline per vector - every datagram sent and received as hex with the source port, every peer verdict, inotify events, /proc process and UDP table observations, bind probes, directory snapshots, file contents read, kills, sentinel states, and every key evaluation interleaved with the observations that produced it) and the state directories themselves; the setup report is the stdout of the setup step.

retained_behavioral_failures.oracle: OpenSSH server and client with fixture-only generated Ed25519 host/client keys and strict known_hosts. Setup queries client-supported algorithms, proves both algorithms actually connect to a permissive OpenSSH server, and proves allowed success/disallowed negotiation refusal against a restricted OpenSSH server. MACs hmac-sha2-256 vs hmac-sha2-512 and KEX curve25519-sha256 vs diffie-hellman-group14-sha256 are forced explicitly. The MAC case uses aes256-ctr and both direction-specific debug negotiation lines must name the selected real MAC. The separate KEX case uses chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com and verifies its implicit MAC, which supplies no evidence for the explicit MAC requirement. Banner is absent because static95 found a pre-auth protocol blocker. Each candidate run requires its own successful allowed command; parser/startup/cipher/authentication rejection cannot substitute for the intended policy obligation.
retained_behavioral_failures.comparison: Exact semantic booleans for allowed encrypted command success, expected negotiated cipher/MAC/KEX, disallowed client status255 at the matching negotiation phase, no command marker, normal server teardown and no forced cleanup. The disallowed policy boolean is gated by successful allowed negotiation and command execution, even when raw refusal text is present. All raw ssh -vv client transcripts, statuses, configurations, server logs and owned PID identities are retained outside the compared tree.

retained_behavioral_failures.oracle: Documented bash-os contract (batch_doc and cron_doc): batch reads a script from stdin and queues ${BASHCRON_SPOOL_DIR}/atjobs/<seconds>.<pid>.<seq>.job whose first line is "# run_at=<seconds>"; cron's scanner runs ready jobs in submission (FIFO) order and removes them; "low load" is currently immediate. Expectations are computed by the observer from facts it controls (submitter pids, wall-clock seconds, the order in which it released each submitter, the fixed consumer clock), never from candidate output. Source note: ids sort by strcmp over <sec>.<pid>.<seq>, so within one second the pid text, not submission order, decides (batch.c:116-119, cron.c:865-892).
retained_behavioral_failures.comparison: Two candidate shells are spawned (the first has the lower pid) and each blocks until the observer releases it. The observer releases them in the stated order inside one aligned second (retried until both ids carry the same second), runs one consumer poll with a fixed clock, and compares the execution order with the release order. The last row releases the higher-pid shell first and the lower-pid shell in the following second. Ids, pids, seconds and the log are retained. Every observation is in observations.jsonl; tables, clock and state files, job logs, spool listings and daemon streams stay in the case workspace, which the harness preserves.

retained_behavioral_failures.oracle: Independent kernel oracle: the helper's own NETLINK_GENERIC client (hand-encoded request builder, attribute parser including the nested operation and multicast-group arrays, several messages per buffer, several buffers per dump, NLMSG_DONE/NLMSG_ERROR/ACK handling, sequence and port matching) is first calibrated on hand-encoded vectors and then on the real guest kernel (by name, by id, dump, two interleaved requests, NLM_F_ACK, ENOENT); it is the only source of family IDs, versions, header sizes, operations, capability flags, multicast groups and errno values, so no expected value comes from candidate output. All peers force non-AEAD aes256-ctr and curve25519-sha256; the actual separate MAC must appear in both raw proposals and client negotiated-direction diagnostics. Setup ssh-Q checks the real client supports both MACs, then OpenSSH independently proves default-allowed, permissive-allowed, permissive-other and restricted-allowed encrypted commands, plus actual restricted-other MAC mismatch/refusal. Candidate repeats all5 probes using fresh fixture keys and strict known_hosts. Standard preserves the revision98 MAC choices; etm exercises another source-advertised real-MAC framing path. Neither variant substitutes implicit AEAD authentication for the MAC requirement.
retained_behavioral_failures.comparison: Exact ordered booleans distinguish advertisement, clear KEX/ECDH/NEWKEYS progress, full encrypted auth/command and policy. Successful encrypted command requires status0, exact marker/stdout, strict fixture host-key verification, authenticated client log and expected non-AEAD cipher/real MAC in both directions. Refusal requires255, the matching MAC diagnostic, both raw MAC intersections empty, other KEX/cipher intersections still valid, no NEWKEYS or command marker. Full policy boolean is gated by successful default, both permissive MACs and restricted-allowed encrypted commands. Raw proposal filtering/early refusal cannot pass that gate if a baseline encryption path fails. Normal server exits, relay thread cleanup and no forced kills remain required. Server phase ports differ; readiness needs the exact Popen child alive plus its own post-bind announcement and the loopback listener, preventing the stale-listener problem observed in109.
